patterns.what_worked: Reusing the house wording the previous lane landed (paladin/warrior/shaman) verbatim, so all six classes now carry ONE form of the truth. The pins match on PROSE (the line-leading comment marker dropped, the lines joined, the whitespace collapsed) rather than on raw source lines, because the claim is wrapped across three source lines in each class file - a flat substring search would never have seen it. practice_ui.lua uses a COUNT (>= 2) instead of a presence, so a note that drops back to the old wording loses its own copy and the count falls. The no-behaviour-change claim was PROVEN, not asserted: the pre-edit and post-edit luac5.1 -l -l listings of all four source files are byte-identical once the source line numbers and the heap addresses (both of which a comment edit necessarily shifts) are normalised.
patterns.what_was_hard: The brief named five sites and said the guard should cover six classes, but the false claim also survives at classes/warrior.lua:4899 - the same FOR THE RECORD note the previous lane corrected in the other three classes and missed in the warrior. That file is on the do-not-touch list, so it could only be filed, not fixed.
patterns.skill_gap: The brief's done-criterion ('no site carries the false claim') cannot be met inside the brief's own scope - a scope conflict had to be reported rather than resolved. Lesson for the next lane: when a brief names the remaining sites, sweep the whole tree for the phrase anyway (a repo-wide grep for 'NAME-first resolution' found the sixth site in four minutes) and file what falls outside the scope.
